rv.q: This season’s finest comedy, “Oh, Mary!,” is making is ‘em laugh just as hard — at Mary Todd Lincoln, of all people!
There’s little else in New York theater right now quite as surprising as “Oh, Mary!”
There's funny, there's very funny, and then there's Oh, Mary!, Cole Escola's riotous new comedy that brings more laughs to Broadway than all the Gutenberg!s, Edelmans and Birbiglias combined.

The playwright might describe it as stupid, but any comedy that liberates audiences from the despair of the current political climate with 80 minutes of almost uninterrupted laughter is a work of genius.
Oh, Mary! is an uproariously inaccurate and queer romp through history without the tiring anachronistic politics of, say, fellow historical romps Hamilton or Six.

They have the perfect director, the right supporting cast and, crucially, enough crazy political chaos going on outside the theater's doors that the wackier this show gets, it never feels too much removed from reality.
This don’t-miss farce is a complete tour de force for the non-binary writer and actor Cole Escola, who is serving up 80 of the funniest minutes you’ll see in any medium!
Escola is magnificent as Mary, a toothy grimace under a cascade of ringlets that warns all who approach: Watch out, she bites .
The joke-per-minute average alone could fuel a decade’s worth of comedies.
Escola's splendidly nasty queer romp has hiked up its petticoats and staggered uptown from a sold-out run at the Lucille Lortel Theatre, goosing a sleepy Broadway summer.
Oh, Mary! is Mary’s show, and Cole Escola is Mary.
Escola has written and stars in this short, extremely funny parody, running less than 90 minutes and packed with more goofiness per second than most Broadway shows.
Oh, Mary! is laugh-out-loud funny from the first moments; though much of the humor comes from Escola's unbelievable delivery and the slapstick combination of actors on stage.

Their over-the-top, irreverent take on Lincoln, Mary Todd Lincoln and John Wilkes Booth is so scurrilously sexual that it is difficult to avoid guffawing at their magnificent awfulness helped by Escola's constant silly shtick and blatant playing to the audience, all of whom seemed to be having fun.
“Oh, Mary!” is entertaining, yes, bawdy, queer, tasteless – i.e. camp – but like an overlong sketch.
What follows from that sequence on is, indeed, sit-com-y with an all-stops-out farce edge to it.
In this master class of millennial mayhem, Escola slyly embraces multiple generations of queer comedy and storytelling.

This new completely original and ingeniously funny play, written by and starring Cole Escola (“Please Baby Please“; HBO’s “Search Party”), turns out to be as hilarious and sharp as everyone was saying.
Once seen, you won’t soon forget the chaos that happened in front of you.
Escola, wearing a wig with sausage curls and looking like Sutton Foster's deranged kid sister, is so delightfully daffy as Mary that it's almost impossible to resist this show's outrageous lunacy.
From top to bottom (and yes, those jokes are included, too), Oh, Mary!'s sharp writing, breakneck pace, and campy performances keep the theater in hysterics until the curtain falls.
Cole Escola’s “Oh, Mary!” is the funniest, most outrageous show I’ve seen this season.

cn.t: Critics hail Cole Escola's absurdist farce about Mary Todd Lincoln as uproariously funny, with most praising its 80 minutes of nonstop laughter and Escola's comedic genius, though a few find the irreverent humor hit-or-miss.

vr.q: Seeing Oh, Mary! at the Lucille Lortel Theater was one of the most enjoyable theater going experiences I've had in awhile.
